To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
erosion of “Kugel mesh” into the sigmoid colon and bladder has been reported for the first time.
a preperitoneal mesh eroded into the bladder and the sigmoid colon, 4 months after a “Kugels” preperitoneum repair of a left inguinal herniation, causing colovesical fistulation.

erosion of the “Kugal” mesh into intrapelvic organs can occur and should be suspected in patients with a history of a “Kugal” mesh repair of a hernia who present with symptoms of septicemia and pneumaturia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the occurrence of a colovesical hernia in a patient who had undergone a “Kugels” preperitoneum repair for a left-sided ingunal hernia.
the occurrence of an unusual colovesical fistulous communication in a patient 4 years after a “Kugels” preperitoneally placed mesh repair of an open inguinal hernioplasty.
the erosion of the Kugel mesh into the bladder wall, which has not been reported previously.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a preperitoneal placement of the “Kegel” mesh is not a safe option and that the mesh must always be placed intraperitoneally.
“erosion of the “kugel” mesh is a rare complication and should always be considered in patients with recurrent groin pain or sepsis following a preperitoneal mesh hernia repair”.
“Kugel mesh” is a safe and reliable material to be used in the preperitoneal space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

erosion of the “Kugal” mesh into intrapenitonal organs is a rare complication and that it should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with septic complications following a preperitoneal inguinal hernioplasty with a “Kugal” mesh.
the use of a “Kugels” preperitoneally placed mesh should be avoided in the repair of inguinal hernias.
a colovesical erosion of a pre-peritoneal “Kugal” mesh is a rare but possible complication of an inguional hernia repair.
The main takeaway from our work is that
“Kugel mesh” erosion into intraperitoneum organs can occur and may lead to serious complications.
erosion of “Kugel mesh” can occur and lead to serious complications.
